articles.title: Xbox revenue drops 10 percent as Microsoft’s cloud and AI business surges
articles.summary: Xbox revenue continues to decline, with Microsoft’s Q4 2026 earnings report revealing a 10 percent dip.
articles.body: Xbox is having yet another tough quarter, as revenue from content and services like its Game Pass subscription dipped 10 percent over the past few months. At the same time, Xbox hardware sales declined 13 percent, according to Microsoft’s fourth-quarter earnings report released on Wednesday. The news comes just weeks after Xbox head Asha Sharma announced a “reset” plan for Xbox that included sweeping layoffs and the spinoff of four games studios, including South of Midnight developer Compulsion Games and Psychonauts creator Double Fine Productions. Sharma has also made some other big changes to Xbox, including lowering Game Pass prices, testing free, ad-supported cloud gaming, and making Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution Xbox exclusives. Xbox also plans to raise the prices of its consoles by $100 and more starting August 1st. “When it comes to Xbox, we are making the necessary decisions required across our content portfolio, platform, and operations to reset the business for long-term growth,” Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said during an earnings call. He added that Microsoft expects “to return the business to growth in fiscal 2027.” As Microsoft ramps up efforts in AI, its cloud business has pushed the company’s overall revenue to $90 billion. Microsoft Cloud revenue soared 27 percent to $59.3 billion over the past few months, while revenue from its productivity business, which includes services like Microsoft 365 and LinkedIn, spiked 14 percent to $37.8 billion. Microsoft 365 Copilot also reached more than 30 million paid seats and Azure revenue hit more than $100 billion for the first time. But Xbox wasn’t Microsoft’s only segment on the decline. The company’s Windows OEM and devices segment decreased 7 percent “driven by lower PC market demand.” Microsoft took the wraps off a new Surface device with RTX Spark, Nvidia’s new Arm-based processor in June, and is also starting to make quality-of-life changes to Windows 11 as it aims to regain user trust. Update, July 29th: Added a statement from Satya Nadella.

articles.title: Razer’s new keyboards drop the price on powerful gaming features
articles.summary: Hands-on with Razer’s new Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic mechanical gaming keyboards, the brand’s first Hall effect boards. The TKL and Mini 65-percent models bring features like Snap Tap to lower prices.
articles.body: Razer has insisted that optical keyboard switches are the best choice for competitive esports stars and the sweatiest of try-hards, but it’s now relenting slightly by offering cheaper keyboards with magnetic switches and a similar array of gaming features. The $120 Razer Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Mini and $140 Huntsman V3 HE Magnetic Tenkeyless, both launching today, are the company’s first keyboards to use Hall effect switches. They’re wired-only boards loaded with gaming-first features, and I’ve had a brief chance to test both and take them for a spin. The new Huntsman boards offer the hallmarks found in many other Hall effect mechanical keyboards, like programmable actuation points, faster key releases with Rapid Trigger, and an 8KHz polling rate. Their linear switches have an average latency of 0.6ms, which is of course very fast but ever-so-slightly slower than the 0.48ms of optical Huntsman boards like the V3 Pro. Razer can stand by its claim that optical analog boards are faster, but we’re really splitting hairs here. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/268673_Razer_Huntsman_V3_HE_Magnetic_mechanical_keyboards_ADiBenedetto_0002.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/268673_Razer_Huntsman_V3_HE_Magnetic_mechanical_keyboards_ADiBenedetto_0003.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The new magnetic models offer plenty of speed at significantly lower prices, as the optical Huntsman Pro boards start at $220, and they have Razer’s full arsenal of deeply customizable gaming features. This includes things like Snap Tap, which prioritizes your last movement input on the A or W keys and makes for easier counter-strafing (considered cheating by some and banned by Valve); Snap Flex, for setting up keys to trigger specific actions upon release; and Dual-Keypress Priority, preventing an accidental movement input from interrupting two previously held keys (like diagonal movement). Those last two features are also available on the mid-range optical Huntsman V3 Tenkeyless 8KHz, and coming to the higher-end Huntsman V3 Pros via firmware update. Do these all sound like pretty niche features for specialized use cases? They are. articles.title: Ted Lasso Sets the Stage for a Soft Reboot With a Kansas City-Set Season 4 Premiere
articles.summary: Ted Lasso Season 4 premiere review: Ted returns with an engaging Kansas City-set season premiere that catches us up with a few key characters, setting the stage for the show’s new soft reboot approach following a three-year absence.
articles.body:
Ted Lasso Season 4 debuts August 5 on Apple TV .

Three years after a Season 3 finale that sure did feel like a series finale at the time, Ted Lasso is back for a fourth season after all. In the modern streaming world, it’s become far too typical for a three-year gap between seasons to become something of a norm. At least Ted Lasso is accounting for this prolonged break in a bigger way, with a semi-reboot approach that feels more akin to a show being revived 10-15 years later rather than one we last saw the same year Oppenheimer was in movie theaters.

The third season ended with Ted (Jason Sudeikis) returning home to America and realizing it was time to stop being the semi-deadbeat dad he’d become, given his young son was back in Kansas City while Ted had been overseas coaching AFC Richmond. Season 4’s premiere is notable, because it’s actually entirely set in Kansas City. Ted is surprised when Rebecca (Hannah Waddingham), Leslie (Jeremy Swift), and Keeley (Juno Temple) show up on his doorstep, hoping to recruit him to return to London to coach the new AFC Richmond women’s division team.

The premiere was shot on location in Kansas City, giving it a markedly different visual landscape than your typical Ted Lasso episode, and it makes the most of it. And there’s plenty of comic mileage drawn from making Rebecca, Leslie, and Keeley the fish out of water for once, as they take in these new sights and sounds. The cast all slip very comfortably back into their characters, whether it be the sweet and funny sisterly connection Waddingham and Temple exude, or the lovably dorky demeanor of Swift’s Leslie.

As for the title character, series co-creator and EP Sudeikis still wears the smile and stache of Ted like he was born for it. Ted’s gotten through the mental health issues that plagued him early on, but we find him at a restless point of his life, working as an assistant manager at a supermarket. He’s still maintaining his usual sunny disposition, but clearly without a true sense of fulfillment. Of course, there’s not a lot of dramatic tension as to whether he’ll accept the offer to coach again — there’s a whole season’s worth of episodes to fill, and we’ve seen the trailers — but the premiere does a solid job of showing how Ted gets to the point where he can admit that’s what he wants to do.

Pushing things on the credibility side though is how the premiere deals with the fact that Ted not only wouldn’t want to leave his son Henry (now played by Grant Feely) again, but wouldn’t want to ask to separate Henry from his mother, Ted’s ex-wife Michelle (Andrea Anders). The solution feels far too easy and convenient, awkwardly handwaving what would likely be a very difficult conversation in real life.

Given the nature of the premiere and how focused it is — no other series regulars appear beyond the four mentioned above, and we never actually see London — it’s hard to be sure how much it will reflect the remainder of the season. But the approach it takes is promising as far as its willingness to lock in on just a few characters and interconnected situations.

While Ted Lasso never lost its kindhearted center, Season 3 was notably overindulgent and often felt lacking in form after EP/co-creator Bill Lawrence stepped back as showrunner. This was demonstrated by its incredibly overlong episode runtimes, which frequently hit a full hour or more in the midst of a show that began with half-hour installments. The amount of subplots and side stories got out of control to the point that we somehow were following the inner workings of two different restaurants at one point on a series that was meant to be about a soccer team.

As we prep to meet AFC Richmond's women's team, it’s definitely going to be odd adjusting to saying goodbye to the entire team we’ve spent the last three seasons invested in, and I do worry that it will feel even more difficult to move on thanks to the show still being set in the same location as before with most of the same support staff in place. It likely would have been an easier transition to send Ted and a few key players to an all new part of the world for a cleaner break from what came before, but even as we prep for these big changes, the premiere does give hope that Sudeikis and new co-showrunner Jack Burditt have learned that less can be more. Ted Lasso needed to feel more reined in again… albeit with a 47-minute runtime. Hey, that’s still short by Season 3’s standards! And while we have yet to meet the new team, the prospect of returning to the Season 1 feel of Ted and his team getting to know each other and once more starting from a true underdog perspective is a welcome one.

articles.title: The Pixel 11 isn’t the best Pixel of 2026, but it’s the smartest buy
articles.summary: Our review of the standard Google Pixel 11 is here. It’s easier to recommend than the 11 Pro, so long as superior image quality isn’t a top priority.
articles.body: It’d be easy to overlook the Pixel 11. Want the best cameras? The Pixel 11 Pro is your answer. Want the best bargain? The Pixel 10A is still a great deal. But the Pixel 11 might be the sweet spot in Google’s lineup this year. With 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, it delivers the same performance as the base Pixel 11 Pro for $899 — $200 less. And while it’s $400 more than the Pixel 10A, it has a faster processor, more RAM and storage, Qi2 charging, and a telephoto lens. It’s also the cheapest way to experience what’s actually new about the Pixel 11 series. With the hardware basically unchanged from the Pixel 10 except for new colors and a thinner camera bar, the spotlight this year has shifted to software, specifically features that aim to take full advantage of what most Pixel fans like about their phones: the cameras and special features that make the phones just a bit more helpful. Last year, we said Google’s Pixel 10 was priced fairly at $799, and that it’d be greedy for buyers to expect more from it. Well, RAMageddon happened, and everyone’s prices went up. The new Pixel 11 starts at $899 and has mostly the same specs. It adds a few exclusive software features that mostly make up for it and doubles the base storage. I guess it’d be greedy to expect much more from this one, too. [Product: Google Pixel 11 | https://www.amazon.com/Google-Pixel-11-Frost-Amazon/dp/B0HBF7RD17?tag=theverge02-20, https://www.anrdoezrs.net/links/8836598/type/dlg/https://store.google.com/us/product/pixel_11?hl=en-US, https://bestbuy.7tiv.net/c/482924/614286/10014?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.bestbuy.com%2Fproduct%2Fgoogle-pixel-11-256gb-unlocked-obsidian%2FJ39TC82XS9%2Fsku%2F6684444] The Pixel 11 looks, feels, and performs similarly to the $1,099 11 Pro. The Pro has a brighter, higher-resolution screen and much more powerful ultrawide and telephoto cameras, but the 11 is just as good in nearly every other way. It has the same Tensor G6 processor, and it even has the same amount of RAM as the base model Pro phone (though the more expensive Pro configurations have 16GB). In day-to-day use, I didn’t notice any performance issues owing to the smaller amount of RAM on the 11, though it’s possible that the newer processor balanced it out. Google didn’t hold back any of the software features from this model, either. As someone who doesn’t upgrade their phone unless they have to (I’m still very happy with my Pixel 9 Pro), I was skeptical that some of the phones’ most intriguing new camera features — Camera Looks and Magic Capture — would be enough to tempt me. Unfortunately for those like me who are holding off on upgrading for as long as possible, both features are rad. Like last year, the 11 has a 48MP main camera, 13MP ultrawide, and 10.8MP 5x telephoto, all of which are smaller and lower resolution than the sensors on the Pro phones. My Pixel 9 Pro’s wide and ultrawide lenses are roughly on par with the 11 Pro’s, and quite a bit more capable than the Pixel 11’s. But in the past week of testing, I don’t miss them as much as I thought I would. Camera Looks in particular helped me have more fun shooting with a Pixel than I have in years. It’s satisfying to quickly swap between different sensor-level presets, and they can make a big impact on how a photo turns out. [Image: The Pixel 11 is fast enough to snag not just a good photo of a Spider-Man imposter on the Brooklyn Bridge while driving by in a car, but a great one. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/PXL_20260813_210704991.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] I’ve been a Pixel user since 2017, going from the 2 to the 3 to the 6 to the 9 Pro, almost entirely because of the cameras. I trust them to take great shots quickly and with little effort. I even brought the Pixel 2 on my honeymoon trip instead of a DSLR, and no, I don’t regret it all these years later. If you’re a serious phone photographer who spends time composing every shot, you’ll probably want to go for the Pro, but for more casual photographers like me, the quality difference isn’t that noticeable, especially with Camera Looks applied. Camera Looks has even encouraged me to slow down sometimes to put a little more effort into my composition. Camera Looks seems like Google’s realization that the Pixel’s default vibrant HDR-drenched look isn’t the best choice for every photo. Now, it’s easy to switch to the bold, slightly more muted “Digi” or the black-and-white “Black Tie” styles when you want to take a more impactful photo. If you like one of the looks enough to make it your default shooting style, you can lock it in. And it’s easier to make adjustments on the fly, thanks to the new quick access dials you can pin to the viewfinder. You can add dials for exposure, color temperature, and shadows. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/velvet.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/classic.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/digi.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/blacktie.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/minimal.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/default.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Magic Capture — another camera feature exclusive to the 11 series — is genuinely useful. The hybrid camera mode records a video and intelligently plucks hi-res photos and video clips from it, and I used it to capture a bunch of little moments with our two-year-old at the beach and at parks. It’s convenient to have a setting that can capture the unexpected without missing a beat. You can also manually capture photos while it’s recording. However, the photos are the highlight, not the video. (The resulting video looks choppier than a standard video, as if it lacks image stabilization; it doesn’t seem like it’s meant for consumption.) I’m more the type who’d like to shoot individual photos, as it feels great to happen upon a spectacular shot. But the AI does a good enough job at capturing little moments in the action. [Image: The Pixel 11’s camera bar is a little thinner than before, and Google’s new Pixelsnap case makes it sit flat on a table. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/268705_Pixel_11_review_CFAULKNER_P1011489.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Another new software component available only on the Pixel 11 lineup is Gemini’s Proactive Assistance feature. It’s meant to handle more of the grunt work of using a phone for things like managing calendars, making reservations, and buying groceries. To actually have it do things for you, you need to give the agentic AI permission (it’s not on by default) to make changes within an array of apps, ranging from Google’s productivity suite to apps like OpenTable, Instacart, Google Messages, and more. It’s partially helpful, but like an intern that gets just enough wrong that you just feel better doing it yourself. In my back-and-forth text-a-thon with David Imel, who reviewed the 11 Pro, Proactive Assistance was more miss than hit. One of the features Google advertises is an OpenTable integration that pops up a Gemini chip to book a restaurant reservation if it sees a relevant message. We could only get it to work by being as specific and formal as possible, including the restaurant’s full name and the specific day and time. That’s not how most people type to each other.  [Image: The Pixel 11’s screen resolution is equivalent to that of the Pixel 10 as well as the Pixel 10A. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/268705_Pixel_11_review_CFAULKNER_P1011482.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Here’s another example of Proactive Assistance in action: I was able to order groceries through my grocery list in Google Keep, but only after I figured out some unstated rules. After I enabled access to both Google Keep and Instacart in Gemini’s settings, I had to adjust the title of my Google Keep list to include “Instacart” (so much for being able to use natural language). Afterward, the feature quickly connected me with a list of nearby retailers that could fulfill my order, just like it does in the Instacart app. Proactive Assistance is intriguing, but I hope it gets better. articles.title: YouTuber Named in Take-Two GTA 6 Leaker Subpoena Insists He Did Nothing Wrong
articles.summary: The YouTuber named in Take-Two's GTA 6 leaker subpoena has denied any wrongdoing.
articles.body:
The YouTuber named in Take-Two's GTA 6 leaker subpoena has denied any wrongdoing.

Today it emerged that Take-Two had issued a subpoena in a federal court requesting information from both Microsoft and Discord as it hunts the leaker or leakers behind the recent spate of GTA 6 gameplay videos.

First reported by Kotaku , the Rockstar Games parent company issued the request yesterday, August 20, in the New York Southern District Court as part of a Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) subpoena. It wants information and records relating to the ‘CyberLeek’ account, which is allegedly behind the GTA 6 leaks.

Every Detail in the GTA 6 Cover Art Explained

The subpoena requests identifying information associated with user accounts that were members of a number of Discord servers. One of the Discord servers mentioned in the filing is 'discord.gg/darkviperau,' which is described as the DarkViperAU editors' server. DarkViperAU is the online name of Australian GTA content creator Matthew "Matt" Judge, who has 2.27 million subscribers on YouTube and nearly 900,000 followers on Twitch. Judge has published detailed breakdowns of the leaked GTA 6 videos this week on his various channels.

In a tweet , Judge responded to Take-Two's subpoena and the mention of his name within it. "I don't know anything," he insisted. "That isn't my editors’ Discord. There aren't even any clips of the leaks in either of my Discords.

"I am confused. I did say he can't drive multiple times, so maybe I caused him to write 'Cyberleek can't drive' on the most recent clips? Maybe he visited my Discord, I dunno. Rockstar hasn't emailed me, I suspect if they thought I knew something personally they would do so.

"Everyone is talking about these leaks, I am not special, hopefully."

Judge then held a three-hour livestream across YouTube and Twitch titled, “TakeTwo Has Subpoenad [sic] My Discord To Look For Leaker (News),” to respond further. Clearly shocked at recent events, Judge joked: “Rockstar just murdered me. I got better though.”

Judge said he “accidentally” showed a screenshot of the latest leaked GTA 6 video on-stream, but he immediately took it down and deleted it “because I don’t want to get in trouble.”

While the GTA 6 leaks were discussed and may have even been shared in his Discord, Judge insisted he had nothing to do with how the videos hit the internet. "I don't know this leaker!" Judge said. "I have personally shared nothing... at least not intentionally."

Judge continued: "I'm hoping this is one hand not speaking to the other hand, kind of thing. As in, the people at Take-Two have no idea who I am and so subpoenaed this stuff not knowing anyone at Rockstar could have DMd me at any time, or emailed me. I have had dozens of conversations with people from Rockstar Games. If Rockstar was truly unhappy with something I was doing, I think they would have just emailed me. Or they would have emailed all of us, because we're all on a community email."

"This has been an interesting time,” he concluded. “I'm sure I'm gonna be fine, guys. This is weird, but I’ve done nothing wrong. No-one’s done anything wrong. It’s just interesting. Definitely one for the history books. One more thing to add to my very very long, strange career.

“And if the feds ask you stuff, don’t tell them anything,” he joked, once again. "Deny everything chat! Burn the evidence!"

"The copyrighted material includes but is not limited to audio visual content, artwork, images, dialogue, or other creative elements," the filing reads. "Take-Two, through its counsel of record, has submitted a sworn declaration confirming that the purpose for which the DMCA subpoena is sought is to obtain the identity of an alleged infringer or infringers, and that such information will only be used for the purpose of protecting Take-Two’s rights."

Neither Take-Two nor Rockstar have commented on the recent GTA 6 leaks , nor have the companies commented on the court filing. IGN has asked for comment.

The subpoena has emerged even as the leaker continues to release GTA 6 gameplay videos. Today, August 21, the GTA 6 leaks stretched into a fourth consecutive day after yet another gameplay video hit the internet. As with the previously released videos, it advertises a memecoin, which one GTA fan recently traced to a Seychelles-based cryptocurrency exchange that might be used to identify the leaker . The watermark on this latest video reads: "HIGHER MARKET CAP = MORE LEEKS."

The leaks come just a week before the release of Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look , which is a timed Netflix exclusive. That’s due Thursday, August 27, and will remain exclusive on Netflix for six hours before it makes its way to other platforms such as YouTube.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI exists in its own universe
articles.summary: Even a slew of “cyberleek” clips popping up across social media and a Netflix timed-exclusive gameplay reveal can’t stop the GTA VI momentum.
articles.body: This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on GTA VI and the state of the video game industry, follow Andrew Webster. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers’ inboxes at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here. How it started Four years ago, fans got a long-awaited look at Grand Theft Auto VI with a huge cache of videos that showed off Rockstar’s latest open-world epic. There were 90 videos in total, providing a glimpse at the next-generation take on Vice City, introducing the game’s new dual protagonists, and generally showing off the crime-fueled mayhem the series is known for. The twist? This wasn’t some official reveal. The videos were part of a massive leak in September 2022 that ultimately ended with a life sentence in a secure hospital for the hacker, and they dropped months before Rockstar properly unveiled GTA VI to the world with its debut trailer. For many video game studios, a leak of that magnitude would be devastating. But not Rockstar: Following the unprecedented success of GTA V, which has sold more than 230 million copies across PC and three generations of consoles, it seems like there is little that can impact the studio in the lead-up to the sequel’s much-hyped launch. GTA VI’s first trailer was leaked less than a day before it was set to premiere in December 2023, and yet the official video went on to garner nearly 290 million views on YouTube.  That’s not all that has happened on the long road to launch. Outside of the leaks, the studio has also been accused of union busting, GTA VI has been delayed multiple times, and the game, which won’t be available on a disc, has been viewed as a worrying sign for the future of physical media. But none of that has done much to slow down Rockstar or the relentless force that is its next game. And next week the hype is poised to reach a new level: A gameplay trailer for GTA VI will premiere on Netflix, available to subscribers six hours before everyone else can watch it on YouTube. It’s a huge marketing coup, and the type of thing only GTA VI can get away with. How it’s going The lead-up to the Netflix premiere hasn’t exactly been smooth. Over the last week further leaks have spread unofficial gameplay clips across platforms like Discord and X, and Rockstar has flexed its legal muscles, subpoenaing both Microsoft and Discord in hopes of finding the culprit. This had led to some frustration internally, and potentially changes to how Rockstar approaches security, according to a Bloomberg report. But, once again, it doesn’t seem to have put a dent in the fervor around the game. GTA VI is so big that even small updates, like a cover art reveal, rack up millions of views. And this has allowed Rockstar to do things no one else can. It can reveal gameplay through a mainstream platform like Netflix, and maintain sustained interest in the game despite only releasing two trailers over the span of several years. “Grand Theft Auto reveals have become cultural moments in their own right,” Netflix exec Brandon Riegg said when announcing the gameplay reveal. “The anticipation and fandom around Grand Theft Auto VI is unprecedented, and we’re honored that Rockstar Games has partnered with us to debut the next part of the Grand Theft Auto story with Netflix members first.” This mentality isn’t entirely new for Rockstar, but the success of GTA V has allowed the studio to be more confident with how it reveals and launches games, eschewing the traditional news cycle in favor of, well, whatever it wants. Back in 2016, on a random Sunday afternoon, the studio released an image that was simply its logo on a red background. The internet promptly went into a craze, correctly surmising that Rockstar was teasing the next Red Dead Redemption, an open-world Western series that had been dormant for several years. That game, Red Dead Redemption 2, went on to sell nearly 90 million copies, giving Rockstar another blockbuster to fill the gap between GTAs. Open-world games have become widespread over the last decade or so, but there’s still no developer that renders its virtual worlds with the level of detail and realism that Rockstar does. That’s true whether we’re talking about a fictional version of modern California or the Wild West at the turn of the century. It’s also probably why the studio can get away with taking so long with GTA VI; fans have been given plenty of reason to believe that it’ll be worth the wait. And that’s why the steady stream of leaks has done little to diminish the hype around the game. In fact, they’re almost serving as a form of marketing; Rockstar may be content with a drip feed of news and details, but anxious fans are eager to soak up every new detail about the game, whether it’s official or not. What happens next Grand Theft Auto VI launches on November 19th, and it’s coming at a challenging time for the games industry. For basically everyone not named Nintendo, things are not looking good: Hardware is getting prohibitively expensive, physical media is dying, major platforms are in a state of upheaval, and ill-placed bets on live-service games have left the industry reeling. There are few signs that things will improve anytime soon. Amid all of that, GTA VI stands apart. It’s a launch so big that nearly every other major publisher and developer is getting out of its way, a game on a scale that has the potential to boost flagging console sales. GTA VI isn’t a fix for everything ailing the industry, and most of its benefits will be temporary for everyone but Rockstar and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive. There are also still plenty of questions ahead of its release, like what the future for the enduring multiplayer spinoff GTA Online looks like, or whether GTA VI’s satirical slant on Florida will still feel relevant after such a long development cycle. But for at least a few weeks later this year, players can pretend everything is normal while they lay waste to Vice City once again. By the way * Despite exploring new territory with the GTA VI gameplay reveal, Netflix appears to be slowly retreating from games. It recently closed two more internal studios, including the team behind the interactive horror story Unhinged. * Fired Rockstar workers are mired in a legal battle with Rockstar, but they say they currently aren’t calling for a boycott of GTA VI. * November is mostly quiet for non-GTA releases, but there’s one game that isn’t afraid to go up against the behemoth: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance + Online. Read this * The Guardian’s “Pushing Buttons” newsletter looks at the challenges presented by hyperrealistic games like GTA VI. * Friend of The Verge Joshua Rivera has a great piece in Aftermath looking at how GTA VI’s outsize importance is a terrible thing for the industry at large. * Bloomberg has an interview with Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick about GTA VI’s “unprecedented” preorder numbers.

It can reveal gameplay through a mainstream platform like Netflix, and maintain sustained interest in the game despite only releasing two trailers over the span of several years. “Grand Theft Auto reveals have become cultural moments in their own right,” Netflix exec Brandon Riegg said when announcing the gameplay reveal. “The anticipation and fandom around Grand Theft Auto VI is unprecedented, and we’re honored that Rockstar Games has partnered with us to debut the next part of the Grand Theft Auto story with Netflix members first.” This mentality isn’t entirely new for Rockstar, but the success of GTA V has allowed the studio to be more confident with how it reveals and launches games, eschewing the traditional news cycle in favor of, well, whatever it wants. Back in 2016, on a random Sunday afternoon, the studio released an image that was simply its logo on a red background. The internet promptly went into a craze, correctly surmising that Rockstar was teasing the next Red Dead Redemption, an open-world Western series that had been dormant for several years. That game, Red Dead Redemption 2, went on to sell nearly 90 million copies, giving Rockstar another blockbuster to fill the gap between GTAs. Open-world games have become widespread over the last decade or so, but there’s still no developer that renders its virtual worlds with the level of detail and realism that Rockstar does. That’s true whether we’re talking about a fictional version of modern California or the Wild West at the turn of the century. It’s also probably why the studio can get away with taking so long with GTA VI; fans have been given plenty of reason to believe that it’ll be worth the wait. And that’s why the steady stream of leaks has done little to diminish the hype around the game. In fact, they’re almost serving as a form of marketing; Rockstar may be content with a drip feed of news and details, but anxious fans are eager to soak up every new detail about the game, whether it’s official or not. What happens next Grand Theft Auto VI launches on November 19th, and it’s coming at a challenging time for the games industry. For basically everyone not named Nintendo, things are not looking good: Hardware is getting prohibitively expensive, physical media is dying, major platforms are in a state of upheaval, and ill-placed bets on live-service games have left the industry reeling. There are few signs that things will improve anytime soon. Amid all of that, GTA VI stands apart. It’s a launch so big that nearly every other major publisher and developer is getting out of its way, a game on a scale that has the potential to boost flagging console sales. GTA VI isn’t a fix for everything ailing the industry, and most of its benefits will be temporary for everyone but Rockstar and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive. There are also still plenty of questions ahead of its release, like what the future for the enduring multiplayer spinoff GTA Online looks like, or whether GTA VI’s satirical slant on Florida will still feel relevant after such a long development cycle. But for at least a few weeks later this year, players can pretend everything is normal while they lay waste to Vice City once again. It recently closed two more internal studios, including the team behind the interactive horror story Unhinged. * Fired Rockstar workers are mired in a legal battle with Rockstar, but they say they currently aren’t calling for a boycott of GTA VI. * November is mostly quiet for non-GTA releases, but there’s one game that isn’t afraid to go up against the behemoth: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance + Online. articles.title: We Build The Massive, Multi-Set LEGO Harry Potter Hogwarts Castle, Currently In Progress
articles.summary: Here's a look at the current state of the "in progress" LEGO Hogwarts Castle, a huge undertaking that's comprised of many smaller sets placed together.
articles.body:
In 2024, LEGO began the most ambitious build project the company has ever attempted: a fully realized, minifigure-scale re-creation of Hogwarts Castle, made famous by the Harry Potter franchise. A single set of this size and scope would be impractically large and prohibitively expensive . So instead, LEGO is releasing numerous smaller LEGO Harry Potter sets that, when combined, will form the full castle. It's a truly massive undertaking.

This is an ongoing project; LEGO has not announced the end date for the final set. But based on their current pace, it's going to be years before the project finally wraps. We've been building the LEGO Hogwarts Castle since it launched, and we will continue building and adding to it until it's complete. If you would like to do the same? it's not too late to start, although LEGO has retired some key sets at the end of 2025 .

Here is every set released so far that comprises the modular LEGO Hogwarts Castle, currently in progress as of August 2026. We've included a grand piece count and price count at the bottom, which we will update as the castle continues to grow. Lastly, we took and included some photos of the castle as it currently stands, so you can see its current progression.

LEGO Hogwarts Castle: Sorting Hat Ceremony

These are the sets you'll need to buy if you want to create your own enormous LEGO version of Hogwarts Castle. But these are just the sets released to date – more will be added in the future.

The Owlery is the first component of the Hogwarts Castle. If you're looking to cut a corner or two and save on costs, you might start with this one, because it's an independent structure apart from the main building. It has winter-themed, snow-capped spires, so if you're after aesthetic consistency, you might also want to swap out a few pieces to make the Owlery match seasons with the rest of the castle.

Both the Boathouse and the Owlery share the same gray-colored hue on their spires. Back in 2024, this led many LEGO fans to speculate that these sets marked the beginning of a new Hogwarts Castle, even though it hadn't been officially announced yet. The Boathouse includes two small wooden boats, so you can recreate Harry's first-year arrival at Hogwarts.

Hogwarts Castle: Potions Class (Retired)

This is the first Hogwarts classroom set, which can swap in to replace another room in the castle. To use an example: The Great Hall comes with the girl's bathroom in the dungeon, where the troll attacks Hermione in the first book/movie. It's nice looking diorama, but it's extremely scene specific, and it doesn't really fit in with the rest of the castle. So, if you want to, you can swap out the troll scene with Professor Snape's Potions Classroom , which is a lot more detailed and colorful, and contains a wider range of roleplay opportunities. If you don't get the Potions Classroom, it's not going to look, at least outwardly, like something's missing. But still, it's hard to imagine Hogwarts without it.

Hogwarts Castle: The Great Hall (Retired)

The first major 'essential' building block in the Hogwarts Castle, the Great Hall includes the eponymous Hall – where the Sorting Ceremonies and Start and End-of-Term Feasts take place – and three additional rooms: the girl's bathroom where the troll attacked Hermione; a narrow corridor; and the Hufflepuff Common Room. The Great Hall connects to the Boathouse at the bottom of the outer stairwell; connects to the Main Tower at its side; and can swap its bathroom with the Potions Classroom. We built and photographed this one at the time of its launch.

This set recreates the Dueling Club scene from Chamber of Secrets, in which Draco conjures a snake and Harry uses Parseltongue to stop it from attacking Justin Finch-Fletchley. There's a gimmicked floor in the table that makes the minifigures fly backwards off of it. If you want, you can swap out the house tables in the Great Hall with the Dueling Club table. It's a fun alternative, but overall inessential to the larger castle, if that's what you're going for.

Professor Flitwick's Charms Classroom lets you recreate the Wingardium Leviosa scene from the first book/movie ("It's Levi-O-sa! Not Levio-SA."). The Professor Flitwick minifigure has his original movie appearance, when the filmmakers leaned into his goblin hertitage. The Charms Classroom slots into the Flying Lessons set, and can swap with the Quidditch equipment room.

On the exterior, this set depicts the scene where Harry rides a broom for the first time (it even includes a minifigure of Madame Hooch). But on the interior, this is a Professor McGonagall-centric set. It includes the aforementioned Quidditch equipment room, but it also contains McGonagall's office and McGonagall's Transfiguration classroom. The Flying Lessons set doesn't connect to any of the current sets; it'll fit in later, once we have more of the Castle completed.

The Herbology Classroom includes a rare Professor Sprout minifigure, plus Hermione and Neville in their greenhouse smocks and gloves. The greenhouse feels appropriately overgrown and busy, with three mandrake plants and accompanying earmuff accessories. It is a freestanding structure from the larger Hogwarts Castle, although unlike the Owlery, it'll be in close proximity to it.

The second major Hogwarts Castle set, the Main Tower connects directly to the Great Hall on its right side. And taken together (see more photos below), you really get a sense of size and scope. The interior contains three of the rooms from the Sorcerer's Stone trials: the Devil's Snare room, the Flying Keys room, and the Chess Set room. One floor up is Fluffy's room and a narrow corridor. One floor up from that is the Gryffindor Common Room. And then the actual Main Tower contains three staircases (two of them rotate), Dumbledore's office, and a secret room containing the Mirror of Erised. We built and photographed this set at launch.

This may end up being the rarest set in the whole modular collection. This re-creation of the Room of Requirement, as seen in Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, includes hammocks and sleeping arrangements for Dumbledore's Army members. It comes with a single minifigure of Neville Longbottom.

The above price of $19.99 is what LEGO listed on their website . It was, however, never on sale by itself; rather, it was a gift-with-purchase for anyone who bought $130 worth of Harry Potter LEGO in the first week of September 2025. Your best bet is the secondary market, but don't break the bank over it; it's an an optional classroom that slots into the Main Tower, rather than a standing structure by itself.

A mandatory set for the full castle build, the Hospital Wing connects to the Main Tower and wraps around its right hand side. It contains far more than Madam Pomfrey's triage center, however; it also contains the Ravenclaw common room and Professor Lupin's Defense Against the Dark Arts classroom, complete with a Boggart wardrobe and phonograph.

This set reimagines the Sorting Hat Ceremony as a wheel-spinning game, and it includes the hourglasses of rubies, diamonds, sapphires, and emeralds that tally the annual house points. It is designed to fit into the Great Hall as an add-on option, similar to the retired Dueling Club set. For fans looking to build the full castle, it's fun but ultimately inessential.

An essential component to the overall build, the East Wing connects to both the Great Hall and the Main Tower via bridges. This set contains the Slytherin common room and Moaning Myrtle's batroom; go down a slide, and you'll wind up in the Chamber of Secrets. In addition to the massive, sculpted head of Salazar Sytherin, the Chamber of Secrets also features a scary-looking basilisk, which threatens to attack and kill all Muggle-born. The set includes 13 minifigures in all.

For photos of the entire Hogwarts Castle build so far, see below.

As of August 2026, the current total piece count stands at 9,778.

As of August 2026, the current total price stands at $1162.87.

In the below photo, I've put together the entire castle, as of August 2026.

I've taken some creative license with the placement of the Hospital Wing. According to LEGO, it's supposed to form a courtyard at a right angle with the Main Tower. But it's impossible to see it, all the way back there, when you're looking at the castle from the front. I could display the castle from a different angle. But if I do this, it reveals the open backs of the models, which breaks the illusion.

So, I've decided to move the Hospital Wing to the area on the right side of the East Wing, directly above where I placed the Greenhouse. If the LEGO designers eventually put the Divination Tower or the Bell Towers in this area, I'll have to move the Hospital Wing again. But until then, I like how its current placement gives the castle better balance and makes it more physically imposing.

I've placed the Flying Lessons and the Owlery on the right side of the castle as well.

Just prior to releasing the Owlery, LEGO released an architectural build of Hogwarts Castle in miniature form. It has the same grey spires as the modular castle, and because of its timing, my theory is that it is a rough blueprint for how the final castle will look. Above, I've circled the parts of the modular castle that have been released. So, as you can see, we have about one-third of the final building to go.

Still, some LEGO fans have theorized that the Hogwarts Castle is complete. The reasoning is that the old 6,020-piece microscale build stopped at the East Wing and never built beyond that.

In May 2026, I reached out to LEGO and asked them if the East Wing marked the end of the castle build. The response I got back was that at the time, they weren't able to share information regarding that.

It definitely feels like the designers could go further if they wanted to. The three most notable, missing parts of the castle are the Astronomy Tower, the Clock Tower, and the Bell Towers. We are almost certainly not getting the Clock Tower because of its canonical placement behind the Main Tower. The Bell Towers are a slight possibility. But the Astronomy Tower would be the most likely (and desirable) of the three. The tallest structure in Hogwarts, the Astronomy Tower is also where Dumbledore and Draco have their climactic confrontation in Book Six.

LEGO announced that a new Mini Hogwarts Castle (seen above) will launch in late August. You'll notice that this build, like the prior mini build, has an Astronomy Tower. The specifications for the set also mention the Astronomy Tower as a key location:

"Kids can relive their favorite wizarding scenes as they build microscale versions of The Great Hall, Main Tower, East Wing and the Astronomy Tower."

We still have no official word, one way or the other, if the modular castle is officially finished. But they've already released the other major parts of the build (ie. The Great Hall, Main Tower, and East Wing), so perhaps the Astronomy Tower is next? Or maybe it's wishful thinking.

We'll have a better idea when LEGO announces the next wave of Potter sets. If there are no Hogwarts Castle sets amongst them, we can assume the castle is finished. But let's hope not.

Be sure to check out our lists of the best Star Wars LEGO sets and best Harry Potter LEGO sets . If you prefer superheroes., you can take a look at the best Marvel LEGO sets as well.

Kevin Wong is a contributing freelancer for IGN, specializing in LEGO. He's also been published in Complex, Engadget, Gamespot, Kotaku, and more. Follow him on Twitter at @kevinjameswong .

articles.title: GTA 6 Leak Subpoena: Discord Says It Will 'Evaluate the Validity and Scope Before Responding'
articles.summary: Discord has countered online reports about Take-Two’s hunt for the identity of the GTA 6 leaker, saying it has yet to be formally served a subpoena, and when it does receive it, it will take a long, hard look at it before responding.
articles.body:
Discord has countered online reports about Take-Two’s hunt for the identity of the GTA 6 leaker, saying it has yet to be formally served a subpoena, and when it does receive it, it will take a long, hard look at it before responding.

On Friday, Andrew L. Carter Jr., Judge of the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, granted Take-Two's request to subpoena Discord to divulge identifying information about users the Rockstar owner believes are tied to the leaks.

Take-Two’s subpoena of Microsoft was also granted. But while Microsoft has issued a statement to say it’s happy to work with Take-Two and Rockstar to help unearth the GTA 6 leaker, Discord issued a different line overnight.

Every Detail in the GTA 6 Cover Art Explained

“I can share an update on this,” Discord marketing director Ryan K. Rigney said in a tweet . “Discord has not yet been served with a subpoena from Take-Two. When we do, we'll evaluate the validity and scope before responding.”

Take-Two issued the subpoenas alleging Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) infringement. It wants information and records relating to the ‘CyberLeek’ account, which is allegedly behind the GTA 6 leaks. The subpoenas request identifying information associated with user accounts that were members of a number of Discord servers. One of the Discord servers mentioned in the filing is 'discord.gg/darkviperau,' which is described as the DarkViperAU editors' server. DarkViperAU is the online name of Australian GTA content creator Matthew "Matt" Judge, who has 2.27 million subscribers on YouTube and nearly 900,000 followers on Twitch. Judge has denied any wrongdoing .

Reclaim The Net, a group that advocates for free speech and privacy, criticised the Discord subpoena in a tweet.

“Copyright law is supposed to target infringement,” it said. “Here, it’s being used to hunt for identities. Take-Two is seeking DMCA subpoenas that could expose users who didn’t leak or upload GTA VI footage, but who participated in conversations within Discord servers where the leak was discussed."

In an article, Reclaim The Net continued : "One of the Discord servers in question has over 107,000 members, and while it is not clear if Take-Two is going after each and every one of them, the request does say 'all identifying information associated with all user accounts' that were or are members of three named servers since June 1 – and that participated in a conversation in those servers.

"In this case, Take-Two Interactive's one filings make it clear that they're not limited to whoever is uploading the leaks, they're targeting entire communities and channels that are merely existing in the same Discord server as those alleged leakers.

"This is now the pursuit of a membership list under the color of the enforcement of copyright. While it can be crushed if people push back, there's actually nothing about the DMCA process that discourages this in a strong enough way.

"To file a claim is cheap and quick, and the compliance cost falls on the platforms. There was a time when companies would at least try to maintain the guise that their targets were limited to infringement but, these days, they're getting more brazen and now hitting anyone who happens to have been standing nearby."

It is unclear if Microsoft has actually been served with Take-Two’s subpoena, either, although according to court documents it looks like Microsoft had already launched an investigation of its own into the CyberLeek account. Meanwhile, the subpoena for Twitter / X has yet to be signed off, but that may simply be a formality.

All the while, the GTA 6 leaks continue , and there is fresh concern that CyberLeek will release significant story spoilers. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two have issued a statement. IGN has asked for comment.

GTA 6 is due out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S on November 19, 2026.

Photo by Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto via Getty Images.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

DarkViperAU is the online name of Australian GTA content creator Matthew "Matt" Judge, who has 2.27 million subscribers on YouTube and nearly 900,000 followers on Twitch. Judge has denied any wrongdoing .
Reclaim The Net, a group that advocates for free speech and privacy, criticised the Discord subpoena in a tweet.

“Copyright law is supposed to target infringement,” it said. “Here, it’s being used to hunt for identities. Take-Two is seeking DMCA subpoenas that could expose users who didn’t leak or upload GTA VI footage, but who participated in conversations within Discord servers where the leak was discussed."

In an article, Reclaim The Net continued : "One of the Discord servers in question has over 107,000 members, and while it is not clear if Take-Two is going after each and every one of them, the request does say 'all identifying information associated with all user accounts' that were or are members of three named servers since June 1 – and that participated in a conversation in those servers.

"In this case, Take-Two Interactive's one filings make it clear that they're not limited to whoever is uploading the leaks, they're targeting entire communities and channels that are merely existing in the same Discord server as those alleged leakers.

"This is now the pursuit of a membership list under the color of the enforcement of copyright. While it can be crushed if people push back, there's actually nothing about the DMCA process that discourages this in a strong enough way.

"To file a claim is cheap and quick, and the compliance cost falls on the platforms. There was a time when companies would at least try to maintain the guise that their targets were limited to infringement but, these days, they're getting more brazen and now hitting anyone who happens to have been standing nearby."

articles.title: [UPDATE] GTA 6 Leaker Releases Game Store, Nightclub and Beach Gameplay Videos, Defends Crypto Scheme
articles.summary: The GTA 6 leaks have continued, this time with two new gameplay videos and a message from the leaker defending their crypto scheme.
articles.body:
UPDATE: CyberLeek has dropped a third GTA 6 leak video today following on fast from this morning's early releases featuring a nightclub and a beach scene — marking a significant escalation in the amount of footage hitting the internet.

This latest release of leaked material also continues to push CyberLeek's supposed agenda behind the leaks: an apparent dislike of the fact that physical media is being abandoned. "People are confused," reads the latest message watermarked into the footage. "This is not about actual discs. It is about ownership. Resale rights still matter — even in a digital-only era."

Fittingly, this message is overlaid on gameplay that shows GTA 6 protagonist Jason exploring a video game store, complete with spoof consoles (that look a lot like PS5) and game cases (I wonder if they include the discs!) There's even a sign in the store advertising "ex-rental games and movies for sale." Titles on offer in the fictional shop include games such as Glory Souls 2, Desolate Rim, We Came Together.

The leaks certainly appear to be ramping up ahead of Netflix's official GTA 6 reveal ( check out the global release times here ).

UPDATE: Hot on the heels of the nightclub gameplay leak, CyberLeek has released a 13th video, this time showing off Jason cycling on a beach packed with NPCs.

This new video includes the same watermarked memecoin advertisement and crypto statement detailed in the original story, below.

ORIGINAL STORY: The GTA 6 leaks have continued, this time with a new gameplay video and a message from the leaker defending their crypto scheme.

This 12th video leak shows relatively unremarkable nightclub gameplay, and includes the now standard advertisement of the 'CyberLeek' token at the heart of the cryptocurrency scheme that is believed to be the motivating factor behind all this.

But this new video also includes a watermarked message that defends the crypto scheme. “Stop the hate,” the message reads. “Channel that energy into protests. Not at those actually fighting for you. CL is taking huge risks in this battle. Leeks are free and donations cover operational costs. Using crypto is the only way. CL can’t win alone. Today is the day to show support and protest.”

Every Detail in the GTA 6 Cover Art Explained

CyberLeek has launched paid-for polls with a number of gameplay video choices people can vote on by sending tokens. People have spent hundreds of dollars' worth of the tokens to vote . This crypto scheme is ostensibly about protesting our all-digital future and Rockstar’s decision not to sell GTA 6 on-disc. At least one person showed up at Rockstar North in Scotland, filming themselves eating a leek outside the office.

There is growing concern that CyberLeek will release damaging story spoilers, with one poll option a prologue featuring Lucia. So far, the leaked gameplay videos have shown dual protagonist Jason only.

CyberLeek has continued to release GTA 6 gameplay videos for eight days straight despite Take-Two's subpoenas of Microsoft, Discord, and X / Twitter as part of the company's hunt for identifying information. We are now just two days away from Netflix’s timed-exclusive GTA 6 reveal, which is set to show gameplay officially for the first time.

From a Take-Two and Rockstar perspective, significant damage is being done. According to Bloomberg , Rockstar still doesn’t know how these leaks happened, nor who is behind them. And while there are no plans to shift this week’s big Netflix reveal, Bloomberg reported that there is frustration and anger internally at recent events, with management sending morale-boosting emails to staff.

Former Rockstar Games technical director Obbe Vermeij, however, downplayed the damage caused by the leaks . Vermeij, who worked at Rockstar North from 1995 to 2009, took to social media to say the Hot Coffee scandal was much more damaging than these GTA 6 leaks.

Neither Take-Two nor Rockstar has issued a statement on the GTA 6 leaks. IGN has asked for comment.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look Global Release Times Confirmed
articles.summary: Here's when you'll be able to watch Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look as soon as it debuts on Netflix, and when it will arrive on YouTube.
articles.body:
Netflix will exclusively debut GTA 6 gameplay footage this Thursday, August 27 via its Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look , which will remain exclusive to the streaming platform for six hours. Here's when you can watch the show as soon as it debuts, and when it will arrive on other platforms such as YouTube.

While the past week has seen persistent GTA 6 leaks hit the headlines , these short snippets of open-world footage feel like they have only scratched the surface of what Rockstar has been building. Here's hoping this week reveals a good sense of both protagonists, Jason and Lucia, and our best look yet at the game's world in high-definition.

The past few months have seen a steady uptick in activity promoting GTA 6 after Rockstar revealed the cover art for GTA 6 back in June. Some fans had expected the game's third trailer to debut shortly after, but Rockstar instead released a big batch of new GTA 6 screenshots , which tease all kinds of new details about the game .

GTA 6 Vintage Vice City Pack Screenshots

It's now been more than 500 days since the arrival of Trailer 2 back in May 2025 — so long ago that when you go back and watch it, the trailer still has GTA 6's previous release date attached to it. But rather than debut its long-awaited Trailer 3 alongside preorders , Rockstar has now confirmed this meatier look at the game, which is now just days away.

Check below to see when you'll be able to watch Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look in your region, initially via Netflix, then later on YouTube and elsewhere. And finally, a reminder that GTA 6 itself is due out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on November 19, 2026.

articles.title: GuliKit’s Switch 2 TV dock gives me one feature I’ve missed when traveling
articles.summary: GuliKit’s Switch 2 TV dock isn’t the smallest you can buy, but for $30, it gives me a safe place to perch my console while I’m gaming away from home.
articles.body: Nintendo didn’t design its Switch dock with travel in mind. Genki’s Covert Dock is a much smaller alternative my family has been using to connect our Switch to hotel TVs for years, but I’ve come to realize I much prefer having a stand for the console when using it this way. So when it came time to replace the Genki because Nintendo broke compatibility with the Switch 2, GuliKit’s updated travel dock seemed like a better fit for my needs. Like Nintendo’s, it provides a convenient place to perch the console while playing on a TV. It’s not perfect, but its few tradeoffs are easy to overlook given GuliKit’s solution is less than half the price of Genki’s. When I first unboxed the GuliKit Dock for Switch 2, it felt like a bait and switch. Although it looks like it’s milled from a block of aluminum like my MacBook, the dock is actually an all-plastic affair that’s convincingly finished to look like metal. Picking it up for the first time was akin to grabbing an empty soda can you think is full. It’s surprisingly light, and while I was initially disappointed, I soon realized that was probably a good thing since I’m an over-packer who frequently deals with overweight baggage. [Product: GuliKit Dock for Switch 2 | https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GZNTFX7T?tag=theverge02-20] The dock’s design — essentially a square puck with rounded corners — is larger than the Genki dock I used to travel with, but it’s by no means bulky or cumbersome. It’s wide enough to securely support the Switch when it’s docked (I actually wouldn’t want it any smaller), and it positions the console at a slight backwards angle that helps ensure it won’t fall off and face-plant even if accidentally bumped. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/gulikitdock5.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/gulikitdock6.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] A magnetic cover protects the USB-C connector when it’s not in use, but while the Switch is connected, the cover can be attached to the top of the dock where it doubles as a slightly taller backrest for the console. It’s a good idea, but one let down by relatively weak magnets. It doesn’t take much force to dislodge the cover, and I’ve already had it pop off on its own while buried in my backpack. Attaching the cover with a hinge held shut by a single strong magnet would have worked better, I think. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/gulikitdock3.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/gulikitdock4.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] On the underside of the dock are four rubber feet preventing it from sliding around and a three-position sliding switch that’s supposed to extend the USB-C connector to accommodate your console when it’s in a protective case. On the dock I tested, moving that switch to different positions only served to slightly change the angle of the USB-C connector by a few degrees, which doesn’t seem all that useful. [Image: The dock includes HDMI, USB-C, and a USB-A port for charging accessories, plus a button that disables the video output so you can just use it as a charger. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/gulikitdock7.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] On the back of the dock is a 4K/60Hz HDMI port, a USB-A port for charging accessories like a controller, and a USB-C port for connecting an adapter with up to 100W of power delivery. Having to supply your own power adapter is the biggest downside to choosing GuliKit’s dock over Genki’s that has one built-in and is designed to plug straight into an outlet. That could make GuliKit’s dock less appealing to some, but it’s not an issue for me given I already travel with multiple adapters that deliver the 60W the Switch 2 needs for its dock mode. Alongside the multiple ports on the back is also a small button that turns off dock mode and video output so the accessory only functions as a charger. GuliKit positions this feature as a way to charge and play the Switch in handheld mode without actually having to hold it. While the ergonomics of that approach seem less than ideal to me, disabling the dock mode does have the benefit of making the Switch charge a little faster if you’re in a rush to top off its battery. [Image: The dock fits in the palm of your hand and is deceptively light, making it easy to travel with. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/gulikitdock2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] If you’re looking for the smallest possible way to connect your Switch 2 to a TV, you’re probably better off grabbing Genki’s or Jsaux’s accessories that incorporate a power adapter into their designs so all you need to provide is an HDMI and USB-C cable. GuliKit’s solution is slightly bulkier, but I really like that it replicates most of the functionality offered by the bundled Nintendo dock with a much smaller footprint. And it’s not just useful for traveling. If you want to connect your Switch 2 to TVs in multiple rooms around your home and don’t need an ethernet port, at $29.99 GuliKit’s is a much cheaper alternative to Nintendo’s $124.99 dock set, even when factoring in the added cost of an HDMI cable and 60W adapter. Photography by Andrew Liszewski / The Verge

articles.title: SanDisk's Zelda-Themed 1TB MicroSD Card Is on Sale for Its Lowest Price All Year
articles.summary: If you hurry, you can pick up a Zelda-themed 1TB microSD card from SanDisk on sale for just $129.99, the lowest price it's been all year, by far.
articles.body:
If you’ve been following the price of tech products lately, you’ve no doubt noticed prices have gone up on things like storage, RAM, and graphics cards. The price hikes have even affected tiny little microSD cards that go into everything from security cameras to Nintendo Switch. I’m not sure why, but the officially licensed Legend of Zelda-themed 1TB microSD card from SanDisk just dropped to the lowest price it’s been all year on Amazon. It’s currently $129.99 , down from its usual $240.

SanDisk 1TB microSDXC-Card Licensed for Nintendo-Switch

That’s the best price you’ll find on any 1TB microSD card at the moment, Nintendo branded or not, so grab it before it’s gone if you could use more storage space.

Note that this is a standard microSD card that’s used in things like Steam Deck and the original Nintendo Switch. It’s not compatible with Switch 2 , which uses microSD Express cards . It’s kind of confusing, but the bottom line is: Don’t buy this for your Switch 2, because it will not work in that system.

This particular microSD card is one of a series of Nintendo-licensed cards from SanDisk. Other storage sizes feature other Nintendo franchises, like a Mario Mushroom (128GB), Mario Super Star (256GB), and Animal Crossing (512GB). However, most of the other ones are either unavailable or overpriced.

The 1TB Zelda one is down $129.99, a price it hasn’t been since last year. In fact, it just dropped from $269.99, the highest price it has ever been. So if you could use some more storage and you like the Zelda branding on it, grab this sooner than later. I don’t think this price will stick around long.

articles.summary: Most new and returning (non-current) subscribers should be eligible.
articles.body:
For a limited time in April, Paramount is offering a promotional deal for most new and returning subscribers that requires an unadvertised coupon. Get your first two months of Paramount+ for just $0.99 per month when you apply coupon code " p2mcs26prem " duiring checkout. I'd definitely suggest going with the Premium tier , which normally costs $13.99 per month, since it is ad-free and includes Showtime. Note that with Paramount+ codes, your mileage may vary.

Paramount+ Premium with Showtime for $0.99/mo

2 Months of Paramount+ Premium Ad-Free Subscription

Paramount+ is one of the better populated streaming services available, especially if you're on the ad-free plan. Several high-profile movies are currently streaming exclusively on Paramount+, including The Running Man , The Naked Gun , and Primate . Its extensive library of media has been bolstered with the addition of Showtime, making it a great service for those who enjoy movies, original shows, live sports, and news. Popular TV shows include Dexter: Resurrection , Marshals (a recent spinoff of Yellowstone), Landman, Star Trek: Strange New Worlds, Tulsa King, Halo, and Yellowjackets.

If you're a UFC fan, then signing up for Paramount+ is a no-brainer. Dubbed "the home of UFC", your Paramount+ subscription gives you access to all UFC numbered events and Fight Nights on demand, from prelims to main cards.

If you watch American football, then you'll be stoked to hear that the regular season starts up on September 9. Paramount doesn't stream very many pre-season games, but that should change during the regular season as more NFL games start airing on your local CBS network and Paramount gets exclusive streaming rights to select games. The two free months won't get you through an entire football season, but hopefully there's another streaming deal floating around by then.

articles.body:
As both an avid tech enthusiast and die-hard deal hunter, I'm a huge fan of Hisense's QD7 TV lineup. The QD7 offers premium features that will sure to please both movie watchers and console gamers at a price point that caters to the budget-conscious. It's available in several sizes, but the garganutan 100" model is exclusively sold at Costco.

For Labor Day, the 100" Hisense QD7 4K Hi-QLED Fire TV is on sale for just $1,4997.97 after a $300 iff instant discount and free delivery to your door. That's not all. Costco is throwing in an extended 3 year AllState warranty on top of Hisense's 2 year warranty for a total of 5 years. That's incredible considering most TVs come with a piddly one year.

100" Hisense QD7 4K Hi-QLED Fire TV for $1,499.99

I love big TVs. And when I mean big, I don't mean 65" or 77". In my eyes, those are average sizes. I mean 90" and higher. I used to own a pricey projector setup back in the day and even had a custom retractable projector screen. After I got a big TV, I did away with my setup and I haven't looked back. Unless you're looking for a significantly bigger size than 100" - like a 150" setup for a dedicated home theater room - you should consider doing the same.

Costco's Hisense QD7 TV won't disappoint for streaming your favorite TV shows, movies, and sports. Apart from the screen size, which needs no explanation for its awesome-ness, the QD7 delivers a great 4K HDR picture with support for Dolby Vision, HDR10, HDR10+, and HLG formats. Hisense's proprietary Hi-QLED panel offers more vibrant and accurate colors and higher peak HDR brightness than traditional LED LCD TVs. The QD7 is also a very bright TV - much brighter than OLED TVs - and punches through even in bright, sunlit rooms.

Gamers will be happy to know that the QD7 is ready for 4K console gaming and is a great complement to the PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X console. That's because it's equipped with a native 144Hz panel with AMD FreeSync Premium variable refresh rate. It syncs with games running in 4K at up to 144fps and virtually eliminates stuttering or screen tearing you'd see otherwise with mis-matched frame rate and refresh rate.

If you're familar with the Amazon Fire TV interface or you're invested in the Amazon Alexa ecosystem, then the smart interface on the Hisense QD7 should feel familiar to you. You'll have access to pretty much every streaming app on the market and you'll be able to control your TV through your remote, any mobile device that can download the Fire TV app, or with voice control via your Echo smart home device.

The vast majority of TVs come with the industry standard one year warranty. Hisense provides a two year warranty. As if that wasn't good enough, Costco's three year warranty extension - for up to 5 years total - means your TV will be covered for longer than most of the other major home electronics or appliances in your house. That kind of product assurance is rare and universally welcomed, especially when it comes at no extra charge.

articles.title: Rainbow Six Tactics Announced, First Single-Player Rainbow Six Game Since Vegas 2 in 2008
articles.summary: Ubisoft has announced Rainbow Six Tactics, an upcoming turn-based tactics game starring familiar Rainbow Six Siege Operators. Revealed at Gamescom's Opening Night Live showcase, and is due out in 2027 for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S. It's the first single-player game in the franchise since Rainbow Six Vegas 2 for the Xbox 360 and PS3 in 2008.
articles.body:
Ubisoft has announced Rainbow Six Tactics, an upcoming single-player turn-based tactics game featuring familiar Rainbow Six Siege Operators. Revealed at Gamescom's Opening Night Live showcase, and is due out in 2027 for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S. It's the first single-player game in the franchise since Rainbow Six Vegas 2 for the Xbox 360 and PS3 in 2008.

And speaking of Rainbow Six Vegas, you play as Vegas protagonist Paul "Six" Bishop in Tactics, who will command the Operators from afar. Tactics will feature 15 fan-favorite Operators from Siege, including Sledge and Ash, and it's packing 47 total handcrafted maps along with 90 minutes of cutscenes to support the narrative. It's set during the collapse of Rainbow between Siege's 10th and 11th years. Development is being led by Ubisoft Paris, makers of fellow tactics game Mario + Rabbids as well as the last several Ghost Recon games (speaking of which, it's high-time for a new Ghost Recon game if you ask me!). Ubisoft also told IGN that there is no in-game store and no monetizations.

Rainbow Six Tactics includes a breach planning feature – which might trigger a memory for fans of the original Rainbow Six on PC from back in 1998 – allowing you to plan and execute synchronized assaults with your Operators. Check back later today for our exclusive interview with R6 Tactics game director Martial Potron.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .
